add.description: Add file contents to the index
add.completeDescription: Stages modified or new files, preparing them to be included in the next commit.

-A.description: Stage all changes in the entire working tree
-A.completeDescription: Stages all new, modified, and deleted files across the whole repository, regardless of the current directory.

-p.description: Interactively choose hunks of patch between the index and the work tree
-p.completeDescription: Allows you to interactively review and select specific changes within files to stage.

-u.description: Stage modifications and deletions, but not new files
-u.completeDescription: Updates the index for files already tracked, ignoring untracked files entirely.

..description: Stage all changes in the current directory
..completeDescription: Stages all new, modified, and deleted files in the current directory and its subdirectories.

archive.description: Create an archive of files from a named tree
archive.completeDescription: Exports the contents of a commit, branch, or tag into a zip or tar archive without including the .git history.

--format.completeDescription: Sets the output format for the archive, such as zip or tar.

--output.description: Write the archive to a file
--output.completeDescription: Saves the generated archive directly to the specified file path instead of stdout.

\u003ctree-ish\u003e.description: Select the branch, tag, or commit to archive

bisect.description: Use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug
bisect.completeDescription: Helps locate the commit that introduced a regression by narrowing down a range of commits through repeated testing.

bad.completeDescription: Flags the current or specified commit as containing the bug being searched for.

good.completeDescription: Flags the current or specified commit as being before the bug was introduced.

reset.completeDescription: Stops the bisect process and returns the working directory to the branch you were on before starting.

start.completeDescription: Begins the binary search process for finding a bad commit.

blame.description: Show what revision and author last modified each line of a file
blame.completeDescription: Annotates each line of a file with the commit and author responsible for its most recent change.

branch.completeDescription: Manages branches within your local repository. Without arguments, it lists all local branches.

--show-current.completeDescription: Displays only the name of the branch you currently have checked out.

-D.completeDescription: Forces the deletion of a branch, even if it contains unmerged changes.

\u003cbranch\u003e.description: Select the branch to force delete

-a.description: List both remote-tracking and local branches
-a.completeDescription: Shows a list of all local and remote branches available to your local Git environment.

-d.completeDescription: Deletes the specified branch only if it has already been fully merged into its upstream branch.

-m.completeDescription: Renames the current branch, or a specified branch, to a new name.

\u003cname\u003e.description: Enter the name for the new branch

checkout.description: Switch branches or restore working tree files
checkout.completeDescription: Switches between branches or restores working tree files

--.description: Discard changes in the working directory
--.completeDescription: Restores a file to its last committed state, discarding any uncommitted local changes to it.

-b.description: Create and checkout a new branch
-b.completeDescription: Creates a new branch and switches to it

\u003cname\u003e.description: Enter the name for the new branch

\u003cbranch\u003e.description: Select an existing branch to switch to

cherry-pick.description: Apply the changes introduced by an existing commit
cherry-pick.completeDescription: Takes the changes from a specific commit on another branch and applies them as a new commit on your current branch.

--abort.completeDescription: Cancels the ongoing cherry-pick and restores the branch to its previous state.

--continue.description: Continue the cherry-pick after resolving conflicts
--continue.completeDescription: Resumes the cherry-pick process once you have manually resolved all conflicting files.

clean.description: Remove untracked files from the working tree
clean.completeDescription: Deletes files that are not tracked by Git, useful for cleaning up build artifacts or stray files.

-d.completeDescription: Extends the clean operation to include untracked directories, not just files.

-f.description: Force the removal of untracked files
-f.completeDescription: Actually performs the deletion of untracked files, required since clean refuses to run without it by default.

-n.description: Dry run, show what would be removed
-n.completeDescription: Shows which files would be deleted without actually removing them.

clone.description: Clone a repository into a new directory
clone.completeDescription: Downloads an existing Git repository from a remote source along with all its history and branches.

--depth.description: Create a shallow clone with a truncated history
--depth.completeDescription: Clones the repository but limits the history to the specified number of commits, saving bandwidth.

--recurse-submodules.completeDescription: After cloning, also initializes and clones every submodule found inside the repository.

commit.completeDescription: The git commit command captures a snapshot of the project's currently staged changes. It allows you to save your work and create a history of changes in the repository.

--allow-empty.description: Allow creating a commit with no changes
--allow-empty.completeDescription: Creates a commit even if there is nothing staged, often used for triggering CI pipelines or marking milestones.

--amend.description: Replace the tip of the current branch by creating a new commit
--amend.completeDescription: Allows you to modify the most recent commit

--no-verify.completeDescription: Bypasses any pre-commit and commit-msg hooks configured in the repository, useful for quick or emergency commits.

-a.description: Automatically stage files that have been modified
-a.completeDescription: Automatically stages all modified files before committing

-m.completeDescription: Sets the commit message for the commit

\u003cmsg\u003e.description: Commit message suggestions based on history

config.description: Get and set repository or global options
config.completeDescription: Reads or writes configuration variables that control Git's behavior, either per-repository or globally for the user.

--global.description: Apply the configuration globally for the user
--global.completeDescription: Sets or reads the configuration value in the user's global config file, affecting all repositories.

--list.completeDescription: Displays every configuration value currently set, from all applicable config files.

describe.description: Give an object a human readable name based on an available tag
describe.completeDescription: Finds the most recent tag reachable from a commit and produces a readable identifier combining the tag and commit distance.

--always.description: Fall back to the abbreviated commit hash if no tag is found
--always.completeDescription: Ensures a result is always produced, even when there are no tags reachable from the commit.

--tags.description: Consider all tags, not just annotated ones
--tags.completeDescription: Includes lightweight tags in the search for the nearest reachable tag.

diff.description: Show changes between commits, commit and working tree, etc
diff.completeDescription: Displays the differences between the working directory, the staging area, and commits.

--staged.completeDescription: Displays the changes that have been staged and will be included in the next commit.

fetch.description: Download objects and refs from another repository
fetch.completeDescription: Downloads metadata and commits from a remote repository, but does not integrate or merge them into your working files.

--all.completeDescription: Fetches tracking updates from all configured remote repositories.

--prune.description: Remove remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote
--prune.completeDescription: Cleans up local references to remote branches that have been deleted on the remote repository.

gc.description: Cleanup unnecessary files and optimize the local repository
gc.completeDescription: Compresses file revisions, removes unreachable objects, and packs loose objects to keep the repository small and fast.

--aggressive.description: Optimize more thoroughly at the cost of speed
--aggressive.completeDescription: Runs a more exhaustive optimization pass, taking longer but producing better compression.

--prune.description: Remove unreachable objects older than a given date
--prune.completeDescription: Deletes loose objects that are no longer reachable from any reference, freeing disk space.

init.description: Create an empty Git repository or reinitialize an existing one
init.completeDescription: Initializes a new, empty Git repository in the current directory, creating a .git folder.

--bare.completeDescription: Initializes a repository without a working directory, typically used for shared/remote repositories.

log.completeDescription: Displays the commit history of the current branch, showing commit hashes, authors, dates, and messages.

--graph.description: Draw a text-based graphical representation of the commit history
--graph.completeDescription: Draws an ASCII graph representing the branch and merge history.

--oneline.description: Print each commit in a single line
--oneline.completeDescription: Condenses the commit history output, displaying only the short SHA-1 and the commit message line.

--stat.description: Show a summary of changed files per commit
--stat.completeDescription: Shows the number of insertions and deletions per file for each commit in the log.

-p.description: Show the full patch/diff for each commit
-p.completeDescription: Displays the actual changes introduced by each commit alongside its metadata.

ls-files.description: Show information about files in the index and working tree
ls-files.completeDescription: Lists tracked files, useful for scripting or inspecting exactly what Git considers part of the repository.

--cached.completeDescription: Lists files currently present in the index.

--ignored.completeDescription: Lists files that match patterns in .gitignore.

--others.completeDescription: Includes files that exist in the working directory but are not tracked by Git.

merge.description: Join two or more development histories together
merge.completeDescription: Integrates changes from another branch into your current active branch.

--abort.description: Abort the current conflict resolution process
--abort.completeDescription: Resets the merge process and tries to reconstruct the pre-merge state if a conflict occurs.

--continue.description: Continue the merge after resolving conflicts
--continue.completeDescription: Resumes the merge process once you have manually resolved all conflicting files.

--no-ff.description: Create a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible
--no-ff.completeDescription: Forces Git to create a new merge commit instead of fast-forwarding, preserving the historical branch existence.

mv.description: Move or rename a file, directory, or symlink
mv.completeDescription: Moves or renames a tracked file and automatically stages the change in a single step.

pull.description: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch
pull.completeDescription: Incorporates changes from a remote repository into the current branch. It is a combination of 'git fetch' followed by 'git merge'.

--rebase.description: Rebase the current branch on top of the upstream branch after fetching
--rebase.completeDescription: Fetches the remote changes and replays your local commits on top of them, avoiding unnecessary merge commits.

push.description: Update remote refs along with associated objects
push.completeDescription: Updates remote references with the local changes

--delete.description: Delete a branch on the remote repository
--delete.completeDescription: Removes the specified branch from the remote repository without affecting your local copy.

\u003cbranch\u003e.description: Select the remote branch to delete

--force.description: Force push changes to the remote repository
--force.completeDescription: Overrides the remote branch with your local history. Use with extreme caution as it can overwrite others' work.

--force-with-lease.description: Force push, but only if no one else has updated the remote branch
--force-with-lease.completeDescription: A safer force push that fails if the remote branch has commits you haven't seen, preventing accidental overwrites of others' work.

--tags.description: Push all local tags to the remote
--tags.completeDescription: Sends every tag that exists in your local repository to the remote, in addition to any commits.

-u.completeDescription: Links your local branch to a remote branch, so you can use 'git push' or 'git pull' without specifying the destination in the future.

rebase.description: Reapply commits on top of another base tip
rebase.completeDescription: Moves or combines a sequence of commits to a new base commit, creating a linear project history.

--abort.description: Abort the rebase and restore the original branch
--abort.completeDescription: Cancels the ongoing rebase and returns the branch to the state it was in before the rebase started.

--continue.description: Continue the rebase after resolving conflicts
--continue.completeDescription: Resumes the rebase process once you have manually resolved all conflicting files.

-i.completeDescription: Opens an interactive editor allowing you to reorder, squash, edit, or drop commits before replaying them.

\u003ccommit\u003e.description: Select the base commit for interactive rebase

\u003cbranch\u003e.description: Select the base branch for rebase

reflog.completeDescription: Shows a log of where HEAD and branch references have pointed, useful for recovering lost commits after resets or rebases.

--all.completeDescription: Displays the reflog history for every ref, not just HEAD.

expire.completeDescription: Removes reflog entries older than a configured time, freeing up repository space.

show.description: Show the reflog for a reference
show.completeDescription: Displays the history of updates to the given reference, defaulting to HEAD.

remote.description: Manage the set of tracked repositories
remote.completeDescription: Manages the connections to other repositories, called remotes, that your local repository can push to or pull from.

-v.description: Show remote URLs after their name
-v.completeDescription: Lists all configured remotes along with their fetch and push URLs.

add.completeDescription: Registers a new remote repository under a given name, so it can be fetched from or pushed to.

\u003cname\u003e.description: Enter the name for the new remote

\u003curl\u003e.description: Enter the URL of the remote repository

remove.completeDescription: Removes the connection to the specified remote repository from your local configuration.

show.description: Show detailed information about a remote
show.completeDescription: Displays detailed information about a remote, including its URLs and tracked branches.

reset.description: Reset current HEAD to the specified state
reset.completeDescription: Moves the current branch pointer and optionally updates the staging area and working directory to match a given commit.

--hard.description: Move HEAD and discard all changes
--hard.completeDescription: Moves HEAD to the given commit and discards all changes in the staging area and working directory. Destructive and irreversible.

--mixed.description: Move HEAD and reset the staging area (default)
--mixed.completeDescription: Moves HEAD and unstages changes, but keeps them in the working directory.

--soft.description: Move HEAD only, keep changes staged
--soft.completeDescription: Moves HEAD to the given commit but leaves the staging area and working directory untouched.

restore.completeDescription: Restores files in the working directory to a previous state, typically discarding local modifications.

--source.description: Restore files from a specific commit
--source.completeDescription: Restores the working directory files to their state at the given commit.

--staged.description: Unstage a file, keeping its modifications
--staged.completeDescription: Removes a file from the staging area without discarding the changes made to it.

revert.completeDescription: Creates a new commit that undoes the changes introduced by a specified previous commit, preserving history.

--no-commit.description: Revert changes without creating a commit
--no-commit.completeDescription: Applies the revert to the working directory and staging area without automatically creating a commit.

rm.description: Remove files from the working tree and from the index
rm.completeDescription: Deletes files from both the working directory and the staging area, marking the removal for the next commit.

--cached.description: Remove only from the index, keep the local file
--cached.completeDescription: Untracks the file from Git while leaving the physical file untouched in the working directory.

-r.completeDescription: Allows the removal of directories and their contents recursively.

shortlog.completeDescription: Groups and counts commits by author, producing a concise changelog-style summary.

-n.description: Sort output by number of commits
-n.completeDescription: Orders the authors by commit count instead of alphabetically.

-s.description: Show only a count of commits per author
-s.completeDescription: Suppresses commit messages, showing just the number of commits for each author.

show.completeDescription: Displays information about a commit, such as its metadata and the changes it introduced.

sparse-checkout.description: Reduce the working tree to a subset of tracked files
sparse-checkout.completeDescription: Configures Git to check out only a portion of the repository's files, useful for very large repositories.

disable.completeDescription: Restores the full working tree, checking out every tracked file again.

init.completeDescription: Turns on sparse-checkout mode and creates the initial cone-mode configuration.

list.completeDescription: Displays the paths currently included by the sparse-checkout configuration.

set.description: Set the directories to include in the working tree
set.completeDescription: Specifies which paths should be checked out, hiding everything else from the working directory.

stash.description: Stash the changes in a dirty working directory away
stash.completeDescription: Temporarily shelves (stores) changes you've made to your working copy so you can work on something else, and then come back and re-apply them later.

apply.description: Apply the stash without removing it from the list
apply.completeDescription: Applies the most recently saved stash changes but keeps the data stored in the stash list.

branch.description: Create a new branch from a stash
branch.completeDescription: Creates and checks out a new branch, then applies the stashed changes to it, removing the stash entry on success.

\u003cname\u003e.description: Enter the name for the new branch

drop.description: Remove a single stash entry without applying it
drop.completeDescription: Permanently deletes a stash entry from the stash list without applying its changes.

\u003cstash\u003e.description: Select the stash entry to drop

list.description: List the stash entries that you currently have
list.completeDescription: Displays all currently saved stashes in the repository.

pop.description: Remove a single stashed state from the stash list and apply it
pop.completeDescription: Applies the most recently saved stash changes to your working directory and removes it from the stash list.

push.description: Save local modifications to a new stash
push.completeDescription: Explicitly stashes the current changes, optionally with a custom message, and reverts the working directory to match HEAD.

show.description: Show the changes recorded in a stash
show.completeDescription: Displays a summary of the changes stored in a given stash entry.

status.completeDescription: Displays the state of the working directory and the staging area, showing which changes have been staged, which haven't, and which files aren't being tracked.

-b.description: Show the branch and tracking info
-b.completeDescription: Includes the current branch name and its relation to the upstream branch in the status output.

-s.description: Give the output in the short-format
-s.completeDescription: Provides a highly condensed, short-format output of the repository status.

submodule.completeDescription: Manages nested Git repositories embedded inside the current repository as submodules.

add.completeDescription: Registers an external repository as a submodule at the given path.

\u003curl\u003e.description: Enter the URL of the submodule repository

deinit.completeDescription: Removes the submodule's working directory and its entry from local configuration.

init.completeDescription: Sets up the local configuration for submodules that already exist in the repository but have not been initialized.

status.completeDescription: Displays the currently checked out commit for each submodule, and whether it differs from what's recorded.

update.completeDescription: Checks out the commits recorded for each submodule, fetching them if necessary.

--init.description: Initialize and update in one step
--init.completeDescription: Combines 'submodule init' and 'submodule update', commonly run right after cloning a repository with submodules.

--recursive.completeDescription: Also updates submodules found inside other submodules.

switch.completeDescription: A modern, safer alternative to 'checkout' focused purely on switching between branches.

-.description: Switch to the previously checked out branch
-.completeDescription: Toggles back to whichever branch you were on before the last switch.

-c.description: Create and switch to a new branch
-c.completeDescription: Creates a new branch and switches to it, equivalent to 'checkout -b'.

\u003cname\u003e.description: Enter the name for the new branch

-d.description: Detach HEAD at the given commit
-d.completeDescription: Switches to a specific commit without attaching to any branch, useful for inspecting old states.

\u003ccommit\u003e.description: Select the commit to detach at

\u003cbranch\u003e.description: Select an existing branch to switch to

tag.description: Create, list, delete or verify a tag object
tag.completeDescription: Manages tags, which are references that point to specific points in the repository's history, typically used to mark release versions.

-a.completeDescription: Creates a full tag object with its own message, author, and date, stored in the Git database.

-d.completeDescription: Removes the specified tag from your local repository.

-l.completeDescription: Lists existing tags, optionally filtered by a glob pattern.

worktree.completeDescription: Allows checking out multiple branches at once into separate directories, sharing the same repository history.

add.completeDescription: Creates a new directory linked to the repository, checked out to a specific branch.

\u003cbranch\u003e.description: Select the branch for the new worktree

list.completeDescription: Displays every working tree currently linked to this repository.

remove.completeDescription: Removes a linked working tree, provided it has no uncommitted changes.
